title: 2021 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final
text:
{{Use dmy dates|date=April 2022}} {{Infobox football match | title = 2021 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final | image = | event = [[2021 Munster Senior Hurling Championship]] | team1 = {{GG|Limerick|hurling}} | team1association = [[File:Limerick colours.PNG|40px]] | team1score = 2–29 | team2 = {{GG|Tipperary|hurling}} | team2association = [[File:Tipperary colours.PNG|40px]] | team2score = 3–21 | details = | date = 18 July 2021 | stadium = [[Páirc Uí Chaoimh]] | city = [[Cork City]] | man_of_the_match1a = | referee = Paud O'’Dwyer (Carlow) | attendance = 7,000 | weather = Sunny (26 Degrees){{cite web|url=https://www.accuweather.com/en/ie/cork/207697/july-weather/207697|title=Weather in Cork City July 2021|date=17 August 2021|work=Accuweather.com|access-date= 18 August 2021}} | previous = [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2020]] | next = [[2022 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|2022]] }} The '''2021 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final''' was a [[hurling]] match that was played on 18 July at [[Páirc Uí Chaoimh]] in [[Cork City]]. It was contested by [[2020 Munster Senior Hurling Championship final|defending]] champions [[Limerick county hurling team|Limerick]] and [[Tipperary county hurling team|Tipperary]].{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/hurling/2021/0704/1232960-tipperary-into-munster-final-as-clare-pay-the-penalty/|title=Tipperary into Munster final as Clare pay the penalty|date=4 July 2021|work=RTE Sport|access-date= 5 July 2021}} It was the first Munster hurling final at Páirc Uí Chaoimh since it reopened in 2017 after redevelopment.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40329602.html|title=Páirc Uí Chaoimh to host Munster hurling final between Limerick and Tipperary|date=4 July 2021|work=Irish Examiner|access-date= 7 July 2021}} Due to [[COVID-19 pandemic in the Republic of Ireland|COVID-19]] restrictions, only 7,000 were able to attend the match.{{cite web|url= https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40332719.html|title=Up to 7,000 to attend Munster final|date=8 July 2021|work=Irish Examiner|accessdate=23 May 2023}} The game was televised live on [[RTÉ 2]] as part of ''[[The Sunday Game]]'', presented by [[Joanne Cantwell]], with analysis by [[Dónal Óg Cusack]] and [[Henry Shefflin]]. Commentary on the game was provided by [[Marty Morrissey]] alongside [[Michael Duignan (hurler)|Michael Duignan]]. Limerick, captained by [[Declan Hannon]], won the game by 2-29 to 3-21 to retain the title for the third year in a row.{{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/gaelic-football/stunning-second-half-comeback-leaves-tipp-reeling-and-seals-three-munstersin-a-row-for-limerick-40665458.html|title=Stunning second-half comeback leaves Tipp reeling and seals three Munsters in a row for Limerick|date=18 July 2021|work=Irish Independent|access-date= 28 July 2021}} ==Match== ===Summary=== The match was played in very sunny conditions with temperatures of 26 degrees. [[Jake Morris (hurler)|Jake Morris]] got a goal for Tipperary after four minutes when he ran in on the left before shooting low to the right corner of the net.{{cite web|url=https://www.the42.ie/limerick-tipperary-munster-hurling-final-5498836-Jul2021/ |title=Stunning Limerick display as they recover to win Munster final against Tipperary|date=18 July 2021|work=The 42|access-date= 28 July 2021}} {{cite web|url=https://www.independent.ie/sport/gaelic-games/hurling/munster-shc-final-as-it-happened-tale-of-two-halves-as-limerick-come-back-from-ten-point-deficit-to-claim-munster-crown-40665027.html|title=Munster SHC final as it happened: Tale of two halves as Limerick come back from ten-point deficit to claim Munster crown|date=18 July 2021|work=Irish Independent|access-date= 28 July 2021}} After 19 minutes [[John O'Dwyer]] broke onto a ball and ran in on the left before shooting to the right corner of the net for a second Tipperary goal and put them into a 2-08 to 0-07 lead. Tipperary had a 10 point lead at half-time on a 2-16 to 0-12 scoreline and also had eight wides in the first half.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishmirror.ie/sport/gaa/hurling/limerick-v-tipperary-live-score-24560742|title=Limerick v Tipperary score recap as John Kiely's side win Munster final|date=18 July 2021|work=Irish Mirror|access-date= 28 July 2021}} In the second half Limerick came back into the game and led by two points at the second-half water break after outscoring Tipperary by 1-10 to 0-1 in that third quarter.{{cite web|url=https://www.skysports.com/gaa/hurling/news/30554/12358557/limerick-2-29-tipperary-3-21-stunning-treaty-comeback-sinks-premier-in-munster-final|title=Limerick 2-29 Tipperary 3-21: Stunning Treaty comeback sinks Premier in Munster final|date=18 July 2021|work=Sky Sports|access-date= 28 July 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://www.limerickleader.ie/news/sport/650126/85-year-wait-ends-as-limerick-topple-tipperary-to-win-historic-munster-hurling-title.html|title=85-year wait ends as Limerick topple Tipperary to win historic Munster hurling title|date=18 July 2021|work=Limerick Leader|access-date= 28 July 2021}} [[Séamus Flanagan]] had got a goal for Limerick in the 42nd minute when he followed up to push the ball over the line from close range after Barry Hogan had made a save from an Aaron Gillane shot.{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/sport/gaa/arid-40339979.html|title=Limerick complete hat-trick of Munster titles with stunning 15-point comeback against Tipperary|date=18 July 2021|work=Irish Examiner|access-date= 28 July 2021}} [[Kyle Hayes]] scored a second goal for Limerick in the 55th minute, running from inside his own half down the left before cutting inside and shooting low to the net to put Limerick five ahead.{{cite web|url=https://hoganstand.com/Tipperary/Article/Index/318584|title=Watch: 'Goal for the ages' as Treaty stage incredible comeback|date=18 July 2021|work=Hogan Stand|access-date= 28 July 2021}} They were eight ahead when substitute [[Mark Kehoe]] scored a third goal for Tipperary late on with a shot to left corner of the net, with Limerick going on to win by five and retain the Munster title.{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0718/1235809-limerick-2-29-tipperary-3-21/|title=Classy Limerick fight back to down Tipp and retain Munster title|date=18 July 2021|work=RTE Sport|access-date= 28 July 2021}}{{cite web|url=https://www.rte.ie/sport/gaa/2021/0718/1235810-munster-shc-final-limerick-v-tipperary-updates/|title=Munster SHC final recap: Limerick champions again after huge second-half display|date=18 July 2021|work=RTE Sport|access-date= 28 July 2021}} ===Details=== {{football box |date = 18 July |time = 16:15 |round = Final |team1 = {{GG|Tipperary|hurling}}
